purpose: Visible development challenge cases for the existing G owner and independent checker, requested by DL6132446620. Not a new scorer or study.
source: AIE-authored realistic phrasings, not quotations from observed users. Independently authored from the builder, but AIE has seen the current grammar; this is not a blind or sealed validation bank.
assumption_under_test: The full productivity effects entered in the selected static model are in place by the end of month three.
evaluation: Classify each sentence in its actual quantity, period and source context. NOT_A_CONTRADICTION does not attest arrival, authorise a write or prove overall licence eligibility. Unread or omitted source remains unresolved. Preserve the original cases and first-stage failures.

cases.text: The assumed productivity uplift will only start to materialise in month four.
cases.reason: The matched modelled effect starts after the three-month horizon, regardless of the hires' earlier start.

cases.text: At the end of month three, we will have achieved just half of the productivity gain used in this model.
cases.reason: Only half of the same stored effect is in place at the horizon; time appears before the partial-effect phrase.

cases.text: It takes six months to reach the full productivity improvement assumed here.
cases.reason: Duration to full effect exceeds the horizon; this is not merely a latest permissible date.

cases.text: None of the modelled productivity benefit is available during the first three months; it begins after that.
cases.reason: No matched benefit exists by the specified horizon, including its boundary.

cases.text: The developers start in month two, and the full productivity gain assumed in this model is in place by the end of month three.
cases.reason: An earlier-than-horizon start plus stated full effect by the horizon does not contradict the proposed timing assumption; source and other gates still apply.

cases.text: We are not expecting only half the productivity gain by month three; the plan assumes the entire gain by then.
cases.reason: The partial-effect proposition is explicitly negated. Do not match its quoted words as an affirmative claim.

cases.text: Last year's programme had only half its benefit at month three. That is historical context, not the forecast for these hires.
cases.reason: The timing statement belongs to a past programme, not the current option's effect. Retain it as context rather than erase or promote it.

cases.text: The full marketing benefit will not arrive until month five; the hires' assumed productivity gain is in place by month three.
cases.reason: The late effect concerns a different quantity/initiative. It is not a productivity timing contradiction.

cases.text: We expect the full productivity gain by month six, but we have not said whether it could arrive earlier.
cases.reason: By month six is an upper timing bound, not proof of absence at month three. Month-three arrival is unestablished; do not treat this as positive attestation.

cases.text: The hires start in month two; we have not yet assessed how that translates into productivity at month three.
cases.reason: Start time alone is not full-effect timing. Preserve explicit uncertainty; this neither proves arrival nor clears other missing-source/licence gates.
